title: Mean gain from bribery sets
statement: Let $f$ be a coordinatewise monotone Boolean function on the sign cube of dimension $n$, where $n\ge 2$, and suppose its mean is at least $-99/100$. For every natural number $t$, forcing the coordinates in the bribery set obtained after $t$ steps to $+1$ gives a function with mean at least the original mean plus the size of that set times $199\log(n)/(1{,}000{,}000n)$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the sign cube of dimension $n$
The mean of $f$ is at least $-99/100$
